text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** The guides I found agree on this, though I only read their search snippets, not the full pages.

| | LiFePO4 | NMC |
|---|---|---|
| Cycle life | About 3,000–6,000 cycles | About 1,000–2,000 cycles |
| Safety | More thermally stable and less prone to thermal runaway | Needs more careful thermal management |
| Weight | Heavier | About 20% lighter for the same capacity |
| Cost | Cheaper per cycle over its lifetime | Sometimes cheaper upfront, and usually more compact |

Sources: [PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)

**Choose LiFePO4 if:**
- You want a unit for home backup, RV or van use, or regular use.
- You want it to last a decade or more.
- It will sit in a garage or hot environment.

**Choose NMC only if:**
- Weight and size matter most, for example backpacking, flying, or frequent carrying.
- You'll use it only occasionally, so cycle life matters less.

LiFePO4 is now the norm. [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc) reports that all 54 power stations in its data set use it. NMC is mostly found in older or ultra-portable models. Check the spec sheet before buying, because some brands don't state the chemistry prominently.
